title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

findings.explanation: The SearchResultSerializer uses Django ORM methods (get, filter, select_related, prefetch_related) which are parameterized and safe. The instance['id'] is used in a .get() call which is parameterized. No raw SQL or string concatenation with user input is present.

The GlobalSearchView uses Django ORM filter methods with __icontains lookup, which are parameterized queries. The query parameter is passed to filter(title__icontains=query) and filter(name__icontains=query), which are safe ORM operations. No raw SQL concatenation is present.

The SearchResultSerializer.to_representation() fetches a Document by id from instance['id'] without verifying that the current user has permission to view this specific document. The instance dictionary comes from search results, but there is no ownership/permission check in this serializer method before returning the document representation. While the calling code may enforce permissions, this serializer layer performs an unrestricted .get(id=instance['id']) lookup.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a permission check or ensure the calling view enforces ownership/view permissions before this serializer is invoked. Alternatively, filter the queryset to only documents accessible to the current user: Document.objects.filter(Q(owner=user) | Q(permitted_to_view_by=user)).get(id=instance['id'])

findings.explanation: GlobalSearchView checks permissions with has_perm() for documents, but the permission checks for other object types (mail accounts, mail rules, custom fields, workflows, groups, users) are not present in the visible diff snippet. The view returns filtered results based on permission checks for some object types but the authorization logic for other types is incomplete or cut off. The view relies on get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() for some queries but not all, creating potential inconsistency in authorization.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure all object types queried in GlobalSearchView have corresponding permission checks using either has_perm() or get_objects_for_user_owner_aware(). Verify that mail accounts, mail rules, custom fields, workflows, groups, and users are all filtered based on the authenticated user's permissions. Use guardian's get_objects_for_user() or similar authorization checks for all returned object types.
